what:
THE ARBITRATION-FANOUT SOAK HAS WRITTEN NOTHING FOR 32 HOURS WHILE ITS MODE READS `apply`, AND NOTHING ALERTED. Found while verifying E17 before acting on it, not by a watcher -- which is itself the finding.
MEASURED 2026-09-24T09:55Z, three independent reads:
  (1) diag log_file arbitration_fanout_soak (#12820): newest row 2026-09-23T01:52:51Z. size_bytes 1,413,493 at /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/arbitration_fanout_soak.jsonl. The last 35 rows span 2026-09-22T16:51 -> 2026-09-23T01:52.
  (2) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE (#12822): process 'apply', declared 'apply'. ARMED.
  (3) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS (#12804): all 11 accounts present including breakout_1, process and declared agreeing.
WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A QUIET PERIOD, read from code rather than assumed: src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py calls arbitration_fanout_soak.record() on EVERY arbitration where a winning intent is decided. record() returns early ONLY on mode == 'off'. It is NOT gated on >=2 candidates -- that is allocator_soak's contract, not this one. So 'nothing contested happened' does not explain 32 hours of nothing.
[!] AND THE REASON NOBODY NOTICED IS DESIGNED IN: the record() call site is wrapped in a bare except that swallows everything, with the comment 'observe-only soak must never break a tick'. That is the right call for tick safety and it makes a BROKEN SOAK INVISIBLE -- it fails exactly as silently as it succeeds. A soak whose failure mode is indistinguishable from its quiet mode is the collapsed-state defect this repo names as a bug class, sitting on an observability surface.
WHAT IT COSTS RIGHT NOW: E17's entire diagnosis rests on this log (apply_scope {breakout_1: 'not_allowlisted'}, starved_count 1) and CANNOT BE REPRODUCED, so that row is blocked on this one. More broadly the arbitration fanout is a LIVE ORDER-ELECTION path and its only observability surface has been dark for 32 hours.
[!] NOT ESTABLISHED, and do not let a lane assume any of it: whether the WRITE is failing, whether arbitration is still running at all, or whether a log rotation moved the file. Three different causes, three different fixes. Candidate to rule out first: ict-shadow-log-rotate.service. The diag read returned 1.4MB of OLD content at the canonical path, which argues against a fresh rotated file existing there -- but that is an inference, not a measurement.
